entries.label: Bridge
entries.description: A bridge, whether it carries the road (passage over: weight and width limits matter) or carries a railway, another road or a path over the road (passage under: vertical clearance matters, as at a low rail bridge).

osm.note: Passage over: on the road way that crosses the bridge, which carries maxweight, maxaxleload and maxwidth.
Passage under: OSM has no tag for the road beneath a bridge. That road way carries maxheight and maxheight:physical, and the bridge above is a separate way with bridge=yes and a higher layer.

entries.label: Tunnel
entries.description: A tunnel the road passes through. Its limits are usually a vertical clearance and sometimes a ban on vehicles carrying dangerous goods.

entries.label: Overhead structure
entries.description: Something above the road that is not a bridge, such as a sign or toll gantry, a pipe or conveyor, overhead wires, an awning or a building overhang.

osm.note: A height barrier that warns of a low structure ahead, mapped as its own feature.

entries.label: Causeway or floodway
entries.description: A low section of road built to be covered by water after rain or in floods, at or near the level of a watercourse or flood plain. Travellers must check the depth and flow before crossing.

osm.note: On the road way. Marks a road that floods without saying whether it is built as a causeway.

entries.label: Ford
entries.description: A place where the road crosses a watercourse through the water, with no bridge or built causeway.

entries.label: Gate
entries.description: A gate across the road, such as a seasonal closure gate, a park entrance gate or a farm gate. Its limit is usually its width.

entries.label: Cattle grid
entries.description: A grid of rails across the road that stock will not cross, sometimes with a signed width or weight limit.

entries.label: No structure (signed limit only)
entries.description: A limit signed on an open road with no structure at that point, such as a weight limit at the start of a road or a length limit on a steep, winding road.

osm.note: The sign itself, mapped as a node beside or on the road. The limit is tagged on the road way it applies to.
